title: I stareted creating a Survival / Action Horror game a month ago, here's what i got so far!
author: cityless27
selftext:
Hello everyone! First time posting here, long time lurker. 

A month ago i finally started working on a survival / action horror game that i dreamt of creating for a long time. Starting out, i had absolutely no experience in Unity or any coding knowledge, but i started to feel AI is finally at a point to actually allow me to create something like this.

So after a month of 12-15 hours of work a day and countless ChatGPT sessions; here's what i've got so far:

\- A shitload of different zombie animations. Seriously, looking at my Zombie animator controller makes my eyes bleed a little.  
\- 4 player weapons: Handgun, Shotgun, Magnum and M4A1. The foundational weapon system supports adding new weapons.  
\- A foundational enemy backbone system that supports adding new enemies.  
\- A complete locked / open / broken door system with key unlocks, item pickup, inventory, storage box, save / load (classic resident evil ink ribbon style), in-game text reading, weapon upgrade systems.  
\- Weapon damage rolls, falloffs with distance, enemy damage rolls, attack cooloffs etc.  
\- An inventory aware enemy item drop system (RE4 style)

My art workflow goes like this: Generate concept arts for the models i want in midjourney, generate models / textures / rigs in Meshy, remesh to optimize polygon counts, bring into Unity and change materials to the Toon shader i'm using. All coding is done by ChatGPT, but i'm trying to manage context drifting, halucinations etc. by trying to understand what is what in the code to the best of my ability. 

Obviously it's still hard around the edges but i'll go on polishing, especially the animations. The setting i'm thinking about is a retro-scifi zombie apocalypse type of thing. Think Resident Evil but in Blade Runner universe. My philosophy is, design all the systems first, then scale and actually build the game. I think i'll work on a puzzle system and a cutscene / npc dialog system next.

My inspirations are kinda obvious; Signalis, Classic RE games, RE4 and a bit of Silent Hill.

Anyways, i wanted to hear what you guys think! I'm pretty proud of what i've got so far but any criticism is completely welcome! I'm still undecided on going more in a classic Survival Horror direction or a RE4 - action horror direction and any thoughts you have about this would be golden.

comments.author: pacchithewizard
comments.body: That pausing every time you pick up items will be annoying, make it seamless.

replies.author: cityless27
replies.body: Yeah i believe you're right, especially if i go more in an action horror direction and keep the enemy item drops. My first starting point was more like classic survival horror, which doesn't have that many item pickups so it's more of a leftover from then. Thanks for the feedback!

comments.author: Belmeez
comments.body: The animations look really good actually. Where do you get them? Meshy?

replies.author: cityless27
replies.body: They are animation packs from Unity Asset Store, from a creator named RAMSTERZ.

replies.author: Belmeez
replies.body: They fit into the rig that Meshy gives you?

replies.author: cityless27
replies.body: Yeah, they are authored as Humanoid rigs and Meshy gives out Humanoid compatible rigs as well, so to retarget the animations i just create new avatars from the downloaded rigged characters and use that avatar for the Animator on zombies. (I even have a convenient avatar / skinned mesh renderer mesh swapper, so i just select a zombie model variant from a dropbox menu in a component and it's done) This works with the single animator controller i have for all the zombies.

replies.author: Belmeez
replies.body: Interesting. I have not had good success with Meshy rigging my models. It always does something funky. Am I just pointing the things to the wrong spot?

replies.author: cityless27
replies.body:
Initially i had various problems with it as well, now i have a checklist:

\- The pack anims must be authored as humanoid.  
\- When rigging in Meshy, humanoid model must be selected and correct height / correct rig points must be set against the model.  
\- The rigged meshy FBX should be imported as humanoid as well and with Create Avatar from this Model option.  
\- Actual rig root game object name on the scene must be the same with the avatars rig root name. (By default it should be, just make sure you don't change it manually)

But of course i'm absolutely no expert on this! It could have sth to do with the animations you have.

replies.author: cityless27
replies.body: That’s actually something i’m thinking about, initially i added that to make shooting more impactful but especially after adding the machine gun, i’m having second thoughts. Thanks for the feedback!

comments.body:
it looks great,

replies.author: cityless27
replies.body: Sure i could try that! I am not entirely sure it would be better though, since i don't want to completely disregard the horror vibe but you're also right, not seeing the enemies at all wouldn't be great. So maybe i could work on the lighting to make sure. Thanks for the feedback!

replies.author: Far_Examination_9478
replies.body: You could add a form of flashlight instead

replies.author: cityless27
replies.body: Yeah, actually there is a flashlight but after i've added all the other lights it's barely visible. Gotta make it stronger. I am actually experimenting with addings some volumetric fog and changing the perspective from ortho to perspective with iso view, that will hopefully help.

comments.author: fatboyor
comments.body: Looks great man! From no experience to actually making a nice game in a month.  what are the tools you paid? Chatgpt, meshy, unity itself? Anything else you think is worth the money? any tools that don’t work so well?

replies.author: cityless27
replies.body: Thank you so much! I am using paid subs for ChatGPT, Meshy, Midjourney and some paid assets from Unity Asset Store (mainly animation packs and some great shaders). I am really becoming a fan of Midjourney to Meshy workflow, especially for an art style like this (pixel art / anime look with toon shaders + some retro style CRT monitor post processing). The shaders i’m using are RealToon and Retro Shaders Pro, both available in Unity Asset Store. Had a lot of help from ChatGPT obviously, but not blindly, i’m having ChatGPT explain everything everything to me step by step and that helped a lot, especially in learning how Unity works. Still a lot of way to go though!

replies.author: GreenLemonMusic
replies.body: I found Nanobanana Pro much better than Midjourney for consistency. I even stopped my Midjourney suscription, so I highly recommend it.

comments.author: Cool-Chemical-5629
comments.body:
Make the rain subtle, its brightness is too intense and confusing. Transparency should do the trick here. You want the players to be drawn into the story and scenery, not put them off with overwhelming visual stimuli.

Another offender is the current effect of the shots. Right now it looks like a camera flash is activated every time you pull the trigger. With single shots it may not seem so bad, but with automatic weapons that fire successive shots very quickly, it may soon become a big off putting offender and you don't want that, tone it down and please, be considerate to [Photosensitive epilepsy - Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photosensitive_epilepsy)
